newsitem.title: GERMANY: Schwarz Pharma reaffirms outlook for 97.
newsitem.headline: Schwarz Pharma reaffirms outlook for 97.

text.p: German drugs group Schwarz Pharma AG on Wednesday reaffirmed an upbeat outlook for the year, saying business conditions had improved markedly in recent weeks, offsetting an earlier slump in domestic sales.
The family-owned group told shareholders it had experienced a clear improvement in business conditions over the last weeks and that it was sticking with full year forecasts made in April.
"For the first five months sales show a 5.4 percent increase from year ago levels to 513.3 billion marks ($301.4 billion)," the company said.
Consequently Schwarz Pharma said again that its earnings per share should jump at least nine percent to 4.90 marks per share with sales rising five percent this year.
Last year the group's net profit jumped by 14.4 percent to 103.8 million marks while sales rose even more sharply at 17.5 percent to 1.19 billion marks.
During the first five months of the year foreign sales jumped 18.7 percent while domestic sales, which had dropped by 10.5 percent during the first quarter, fell only eight percent.
Schwarz Pharma, like many German drugs groups, had felt the pinch of Germany's health reforms requiring physicians to prescribe the cheapest medication wherever possible.
In light of these problems, Schwarz Pharma has been active in forging alliances abroad, particularly in the U.S., to help increase sales in more lucrative markets.

Schwarz Pharma shares, which have been considered a market darling since they were floated nearly two years ago dipped 0.5 percent in bourse trading to 126.80 marks, still outperforming the overall DAX index of German blue-chips which was down over one percent.
Earlier analysts had said they were concerned that Schwarz Pharma might face considerable pressure on some of its products in the near-term.
